summary: FireWatch is a geospatial intelligence platform that reconciles over 20 years of NASA MODIS active fire records (1 km) with the superior spatial resolution of VIIRS (375 m – 750 m). Through a Python regression and scaling pipeline, we generate a "Harmonized MODIS" dataset cross-validated against co-located, simultaneous VIIRS detections at a 80% confidence level. This unified time series powers a machine learning model that analyzes thermal anomalies and recurrence patterns to forecast when and where ignitions are most likely to occur, delivering actionable early warnings to first responders, civil protection authorities and local communities.
details:
FireWatch Harmonizer is a full-stack Earth observation and field-intelligence application that combines NASA satellite data, statistical physics, and off-grid communications to harmonize wildfire records and support frontline emergency response. It ingests Fire Radiative Power (FRP) data from MODIS (1 km, 2000–present) and VIIRS (375 m, 2012–present), aligns them on standardized spatial grids via a Medallion Lakehouse pipeline, and reconstructs continuous radiative histories validated through Spatial Block Cross-Validation and logarithmic quantiles.

The benefits are physical consistency and reliability: traditional polynomial baselines underestimate total radiative energy by over 20% (0.7949 energy ratio), while piecewise models create artificial jumps and negative values. Our Poisson-deviance model eliminates negative predictions, improves global energy bias to 0.9867 (R2=0.7707R^2, RMSE=2065.60 MW), and quantifies megafire dispersion without synthetic hotspots. Its impact is giving climate scientists and rural brigades a trustworthy, connectivity-resilient tool to prioritize rapid intervention.

We built the project with Python (scikit-learn, HistGradientBoostingRegressor, DuckDB, PostGIS, GeoParquet, FastAPI), a Vite/JavaScript geospatial dashboard. Our core engine uses a Gradient Boosted Decision Tree with Poisson deviance and log1p quantile regression to model heteroscedastic wildfire variance accurately without spatial data leakage.

We turns two decades of fire data into an explainable, reproducible system. We balanced rigor and usability by delivering an interactive multi-model explorer (Polynomial, Piecewise, and GBDT Poisson), spatial uncertainty maps, and offline alerts accessible in the field.
